1 Fortasse Ptolemaeus ; cf. Tetrab., I, 9. At cf. Vettium Valentem, l. II, c. 11
(Περὶ χρόνων ἐμπράκτων) : ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ συγγραφεὺς ἔφη, et l. IV, c. 31 (f. 78v,
cod. Hamb.): καὶ κατὰ τὸν συγγραφέα· οὐ γὰρ πάντες ἄνθρωποι ... ubi ⸢ scriptor ⸥
Hermes Trismegistus esse videtur. Nam Thot, litterarum inventor, primus libros
composuisse fertur.
sections.en: 1 Perhaps Ptolemy ; compare Tetrabiblos, I, 9. But compare Vettius Valens, book II, chapter 11 (Περὶ χρόνων ἐμπράκτων ('On active times')) : ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ συγγραφεὺς ἔφη ('likewise also the writer said'), and book IV, chapter 31 (f. 78v, cod. Hamb.): καὶ κατὰ τὸν συγγραφέα· οὐ γὰρ πάντες ἄνθρωποι ... ('and according to the writer: for not all men ...') where ⸢ the writer ⸥ seems to be Hermes Trismegistus. For Thoth, the inventor of letters, is said to have been the first to compose books.

summary.headline: Fixed Stars and Planetary Affinities
summary.text: Astrological discussion of bright fixed stars at birth, their affinities and mixtures with the planets, Sun, and Moon, and their corresponding effects. The author cites Ptolemy’s astronomical material and announces a new diagrammatic table of celestial bodies, while notes discuss Vettius Valens, Hermes Trismegistus, and Thoth.
